Sonu then explains why Washington’s path of least resistance is more spending no matter who wins, which means more debt and potentially higher rates, but also more profits for the private sector in the short term. Ryan reminds listeners that stocks have done well under Obama, Trump 1.0, and Biden, even when many people disliked the president, and closes with a notable stat: the S&P 500 was higher 12 months after all 19 midterm elections since World War II. They still see a global bull market with life left in it, and encourage listeners to stick to their plan and go vote.
